overview: White develops the queen's knight and keeps Nf3 or Bg5 flexible. Black usually plays 3...e6, then ...d5 (Stonewall) or ...Bb4 (Nimzo-Dutch), or 3...g6 for the Leningrad. Black fights for e4 and a kingside attack with ...f5 and pieces; White aims for e4 and a queenside edge.

white_ideas.idea: Nf3, g3 and Bg2 fianchetto, aiming for e4.
4.Bg5 or 4.e3 to stop the Nimzo-Dutch ...Bb4 ideas or exploit the e5 square.

black_ideas.idea: Control e4 with ...f5 and ...Nf6, then a kingside attack after ...Qe8-h5.
Stonewall set-up with ...d5, ...c6 and ...Bd6, or Leningrad ...g6 and ...Bg7.

typical_structures.structure: Stonewall: pawns c6, d5, e6, f5 with a bishop on d6.

character.notes: Dutch reputation: unbalanced, weakened e8-h5 diagonal and e5, mutual kingside tactics.

soundness.notes: Sound at all levels, though White keeps a small edge in theory.

structure.notes: Stonewall or Leningrad pawn chains lock the centre; play moves to the wings.

level.notes: Weak squares and plans need understanding; not forcing theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Leningrad
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 f5 2. c4 Nf6 3. Nc3 g6

sublines_that_differ.name: Nimzo-Dutch
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 f5 2. c4 Nf6 3. Nc3 e6 4. Nf3 Bb4
sublines_that_differ.how: Pins the knight, fights for e4.

character.reason: Dutch positions are unbalanced with mutual kingside risks.

structure.reason: Stonewall and Leningrad lock the centre; play is on the wings.

approach.reason: A recognised defence played by strong players.

level.reason: Plans and weak squares matter more than memory.

plans.reason: Black plays for a kingside attack, often with a Stonewall.
